reason: Both describe the identical root cause: the subquery uses status = 'failed' instead of status != 'failed', inverting the intended filter so latestBacklog keys off the most recent failed run rather than excluding failed runs. Both note the same two runtime consequences — when no failed run exists, the correlated MAX(id) is NULL and the query returns nothing (empty backlog), and when a failed run does exist, it wrongly takes precedence over the last real observation. The reviewer's finding is a verified paraphrase of the same mechanism, not a different bug or vague complaint."
